title: EXP-063 - Hello World Part 4 Section 5: Import Item Pictures at Runtime on FX_Items
objective: Follow hello-world-pt4.md Section 5 (05:13–05:51) on the runtime FX_Items Form built in EXP-062-R4. For each of the three existing records, select the record, activate the Import button (Primary event FX_ImportPicture, Binary Value Action Import into FX_PictureStatic), and in the native file chooser supply the operator-provided PNG whose name matches the Item: dumbbell -> C:\AI\mongoose-factory\assets\dumbbell.png, eggs -> C:\AI\mongoose-factory\assets\eggs.png, guitar -> C:\AI\mongoose-factory\assets\guitar.png. The three records already hold the same pictures, imported and saved manually by the operator, so this run overwrites them; it tests whether the worker can perform the import. Verify each picture appears in the picture Static and that the record shows as modified. Then perform exactly one runtime Save, verify the clean state, close and reopen the runtime Form once, and verify that each record displays its own picture. Change no other field, record, Form or object. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt4.md Section 5 (05:13–05:51) and the EXP-062-R4 record and evidence (T13 runtime check) before browser interaction.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-063-hello-world-part-4-section-5-import-item-pictures.md and evidence/EXP-063/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.
Use the existing authenticated session without reauthentication, refresh, restart or configuration change. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection.

In the Web Client, record the open runtime Forms and their dirty state. Open the FX_Items runtime Form once through Form > Open > Select Form (or reuse a clean open FX_Items Form) and verify the Form identity, three records (dumbbell, eggs, guitar), the visible Import button, the picture Static showing the picture the operator imported and saved earlier (record what each record shows) and runtime Save disabled.

For each record in the order dumbbell, eggs, guitar: select the record through its grid row; verify the Item value; click the Import button once; when the native file chooser appears, supply exactly the matching file path with the browser file-upload tool; verify the record becomes marked modified (orange diamond) and the picture Static shows the picture. Because the same file is re-imported, an unchanged-looking picture is expected; the proof is the file chooser, the upload result and the modified marker. Never supply a file to a different record.

If the file chooser does not appear, the upload tool is unavailable or refused, the Import action shows an error, the record does not become modified, or the picture disappears, stop blocked before any Save and record the exact message.
After all three imports, verify each record still shows its own picture when reselected, and no other field changed.
Perform exactly one runtime Save through the native toolbar Save. Record the native response verbatim and verify the clean state (Save disabled, no modified markers).
Close the clean FX_Items runtime Form once and reopen it once through Form > Open > Select Form. Verify each of the three records displays its own picture after the reopen.
Capture screenshots that show the Item value together with its picture for each record, before Save, after Save and after the reopen.
Leave the Designer untouched and the FX_Items IDO checkout as it is.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.
out_of_scope: Any Designer change, Form definition change, Save in the Designer or Form-level edit.
Changing any field other than the picture through the Import action, or creating, deleting or editing records.
Supplying any file other than the three named PNGs from the assets folder, or a file to the wrong record.
Exporting pictures, or any other Binary Value Action.
Changing the FX_Items IDO, its checkout, property classes, SQL tables, strings or other tenant objects.
Any unload, cache, FormSync, deployment or preference operation.
Browser JavaScript, console or network inspection, direct URL navigation, refresh or restart.
Modifying earlier experiment records, AGENTS.md, tutorial sources, recipes or files outside the EXP-063 paths, and the assets folder itself.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Never change a record field other than the picture set by the Import action.
Never supply a picture file to a record whose Item value does not match the file name.
Never invoke runtime Save more than once or retry an uncertain Save.
Never close a dirty Form or discard changes without operator approval.
Never open or change anything in the Designer.
Never click the Designer top-toolbar Delete button (Delete Form Definition).
Never perform check-in, undo checkout or other checkout-management actions.
Never perform any unload, cache, FormSync or deployment action.
Never use direct SQL, scripts, application internals or browser JavaScript.
Never reauthenticate, refresh, restart or replace the browser session.
Never repeat an uncertain import, Save, close or reopen.
Never claim database durability beyond the observed close/reopen recovery.
prohibited_patterns: \b(?:Unload All Global Form Objects|Unload IDO Metadata)\b

acceptance_checks.description: Sources reviewed; session usable without challenge; the runtime FX_Items Form is open with verified identity, the three records dumbbell, eggs and guitar, the visible Import button, the picture Static showing the operator-saved picture for each record, and Save disabled. Evidence: tab list, open route, identity and three-record screenshots.

For dumbbell: record selected and verified; one Import click opened the native file chooser; exactly C:\AI\mongoose-factory\assets\dumbbell.png was supplied; the record became marked modified and the picture Static shows the picture (same file as the operator import, so it may look unchanged). Evidence: before/after screenshots showing Item value and picture, audit of the upload call. The upload tool result is the decisive proof of the worker import.
Same as AC-2 for eggs with C:\AI\mongoose-factory\assets\eggs.png. Evidence: before/after screenshots, upload audit. The upload tool result is the decisive proof of the worker import.
Same as AC-2 for guitar with C:\AI\mongoose-factory\assets\guitar.png. Evidence: before/after screenshots, upload audit. The upload tool result is the decisive proof of the worker import.

Before Save, reselecting each record shows its own picture, and no other field changed (Item, Description, Cost, Unit of Measure match the EXP-062-R4 T13 values). Evidence: per-record screenshots and field readbacks.
Exactly one runtime Save; the native response is recorded verbatim; Save becomes disabled and no modified markers remain. Evidence: pre/post-Save screenshots, Save count.
The clean runtime Form is closed once and reopened once; each of the three records displays its own picture after the reopen. Evidence: reopen route, three per-record screenshots after reopen.

The final EXP-063 report gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-7, the complete action audit with exact counts (three Import clicks, three uploads, one Save, one close/reopen, zero Designer actions, zero other field edits), the worker-written-file inventory and the final state. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are observed only.

Confirm that the browser file-upload tool is listed among your available tools, without calling it.
